speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes; these are concerning symptoms for a systemic condition. To begin our investigation, have you noticed any specific changes in your bowel habits, such as blood in the stool or unexplained diarrhea?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms of significant weight loss, drenching night sweats, and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy are highly concerning for a systemic process like lymphoma. In addition to your abdominal pain, have you experienced any fever, or any difficulty swallowing or food sticking in your throat?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a "fixed," painless, and rapidly enlarging supraclavicular node is a classic "B symptom" for lymphoma. To further assess the extent of your abdominal pain and potential organ involvement, do you have any pain in your right upper quadrant or jaundice? REQUEST TEST: CBC, LDH, and ESR.

text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC (Elevated), Hemoglobin (Slightly Decreased), Platelets (Normal); Lactate_Dehydrogenase (Elevated); ESR: Not available in provided data.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.
